column3: Value
console_app

Launch Visual Studio; create a C# Console App via the All-languages filter; capture the default selected target framework; create the project; open the project Properties and validate Output type is 'Console Application' and the target framework matches the captured value; double-click the project node and validate the .csproj <TargetFramework>; build the solution and verify 'Build succeeded'; click the toolbar Run button and validate the console output; then close Visual Studio. NOTE: several selectors here are Visual Studio version / UI-language dependent (language-filter combo, console-app template, Properties output-type/framework fields, the .csproj document, the Run button, and the spawned console window) and are flagged in the Expected column as needing live tuning.

column3: Open Start menu via Win key.
Type 'Visual Studio' into Start menu search.
Press Enter to launch Visual Studio.
column15: Visual Studio opens.

column3: Locate the VS main window; stash hwnd in vars.vs_hwnd.
Maximize the Visual Studio main window.
Find 'Create a new project' button on the Start Window.
Click 'Create a new project'.
Set the Language filter ComboBox to 'All _languages' via UIA.
column15: Language filter set to All languages (item name carries the mnemonic underscore 'All _languages').

column3: Find the template search box.
Click the search box.
Type the template name into the search box.
Press Enter to submit the search.
Find the C# Console App template in results.
column15: LIVE-TUNE: with All-languages filter the top exact 'Console App' result is the C# .NET template (detail pane tags C# / Console); nth 1 picks it ahead of the F#/VB duplicates and 'Console App (.NET Framework)'.

column3: Click the Console App template.
Find the Next button (template page).
Click Next to go to project configuration.
Find the Next button (configuration page).
Click Next to go to Additional Information.
Read the full selected target-framework value into vars.selected_framework.
column15: Additional Information framework ComboBox (name '_Framework'); read_text uses selected_text() for ComboBox. Full value e.g. '.NET 10.0 (Long Term Support)' - recorded for the log.

column3: Extract the framework version token (e.g. '10.0') into vars.fw_ver for cross-format validation.
column15: Version token is the shared substring across the Properties combo ('.NET 10.0'), the Additional Info combo, and the .csproj moniker ('net10.0') - used to validate consistency without format mismatch.

Click Create to generate the project.
column15: Console App project is created and loads.

Click the View menu.
Find Solution Explorer menu item.
